profile.reading: EdgeCore Silicon Valley is a two building campus in Santa Clara, California, comprising EdgeCore Silicon Valley SV01 at 3580 Juliette Lane and EdgeCore Silicon Valley SV02 at 2201 Laurelwood Road, both zip code 95054, per a facility specific aggregator listing naming both addressed buildings that together form the campus. This registry carries only a single row for the shared campus and could not confirm which specific building this row's own mapped polygon represents, so both addresses are recorded together as the campus location rather than attributed to only one building. EdgeCore's own Silicon Valley locations page describes the campus as totaling 540,000 square feet across the two buildings on a 12 acre site, with 72 megawatts of critical IT load, designed to LEED certification standards with a power usage effectiveness rating under 1.3 and a water usage effectiveness rating under 0.01. Santa Clara, home to Intel Corporation's headquarters, sits at the center of Silicon Valley's dense data center and technology corridor, alongside major campuses operated by Equinix, Digital Realty, CoreSite, and Evocative already on file elsewhere in this registry, drawing power from Silicon Valley Power, the city owned municipal utility, and Pacific Gas and Electric in surrounding areas, both interconnected to the CAISO grid. EdgeCore is a hyperscale data center developer and operator building large scale campuses for cloud and enterprise tenants requiring substantial critical IT load, with additional campuses including a Mesa, Arizona site already on file elsewhere in this registry. EdgeCore's stated sub 1.3 power usage effectiveness and sub 0.01 water usage effectiveness targets reflect a broader industry trend among newer hyperscale campus developers toward air cooled or minimal water use designs, particularly relevant in California given the state's recurring drought conditions and the added regulatory scrutiny data center water consumption has drawn from state and local water agencies in recent years.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Silicon Valley publishes 72 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this supports roughly 1,800 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation average, it supports roughly 7,200 racks.

The 540,000 square feet of technical space is large enough to accommodate dense cooling infrastructure alongside compute, which matters for high-heat GPU deployments. The operator does not publish a per-rack power envelope or a cooling specification, so the actual density and thermal design of this facility remain unclear from public sources.

The campus holds a single published certification, LEED, which addresses the efficiency of the building envelope and mechanical systems. LEED says nothing about uptime tier, redundancy architecture, or security posture, none of which are published on the operator's specification page.

Among the 103 data center facilities mapped in California, only five have published a megawatt figure. EdgeCore Silicon Valley's 72 MW ranks second among those five, representing 42 percent of the confirmed published capacity in the state. That share reflects sparse industry disclosure rather than a census of California's actual installed base, which is substantially larger than the 170 MW this site has read.
